spec.title: Catalogue: the seams of an Eclipse Theia upstream a delta can use

status.comment: edition 1.0.0; example locations were verified on upstream master c8926e4d (version 1.75.0) on 2026-09-09 and are cited as paths and line numbers only, never as code

p.SEAM-CATALOGUE-IS-A-MENU-NOT-AN-INSTANCE: This catalogue lists the ways an Eclipse Theia monorepo itself lets a product add or change behaviour, ranked by how far upstream sanctions them. It is a **menu**: a product picks from it the seams its delta actually leans on and records those, dated to its pin, as its own seam map (`MI-SEAM-MAP-REQUIRED`); the map is an instance that lives in the product and names the product's interventions, this catalogue names neither.

p.SEAM-CATALOGUE-EXAMPLES-ARE-LOCATIONS-NO: Every example here is a path and, where useful, a line number on one upstream commit. The catalogue quotes no upstream code: a location is a fact about where a seam sits, code would be a copy of someone else's work. A location that moved on a newer pin is a reason to re-validate the row, not the seam.

p.SEAM-CATALOGUE-ORDER: Tiers run from the most sanctioned to the least: a change upstream itself accepts, the data upstream reads, upstream's own extension mechanisms, the composition of an application, a hook in an upstream body, types, the build and hygiene registries, and finally the internals of an upstream module. A new intervention looks for the highest tier that expresses it (`MI-SEAM-MAP-IS-RANKED`).

p.SEAM-ADDITIONS-NEED-NO-PATCH: The one fact that reorders everything else for this family: **an addition needs no upstream edit at all.** Own code is an npm package with a `theiaExtensions` array; an application includes it by one line of its own `dependencies`; the application's generator emits the container load for it. There is no central import list to graft into and no registry file to edit, so tiers 4 and above are rare events here, and a seam map that names one has to say what forced it.

p.SEAM-UPSTREAM-PR: A pull request upstream that parameterises a behaviour by the application's configuration costs nothing after it merges, and this upstream already parameterises a great deal that way — the whole `theia` section of an application manifest is a schema of such parameters (`dev-packages/application-package/src/application-props.ts:286-336`). Use it for the few behaviours a product wants clean at the source; the release train is monthly, so a merged parameter is usually available within one upgrade cycle.

tier-1.title: Tier 1 — data upstream reads, no code

facts.SEAM-APPLICATION-MANIFEST: The application's `package.json` is the widest seam of this family and the file a product owns outright: the `theia` section carries `target`, `frontend.config` (the application name, the default icon theme, the default locale, preference defaults, the Electron window options and `appUserModelId`) and `backend.config`; `productName`, `main`, `theiaPluginsDir` and the `dependencies` inventory of extensions sit beside it (`examples/electron/package.json:1-29`; the schema at `dev-packages/application-package/src/application-props.ts:133-336`). There is no `product.json` and no development sidecar: the values are frozen into `src-gen/` at build time. Codkit layer: config-overlay with `expectUpstream`.
facts.SEAM-APPLICATION-NAME: Product identity is one key, `theia.frontend.config.applicationName`. It is emitted into the generated frontend entry (`dev-packages/application-manager/src/generator/frontend-generator.ts:80-82`), used as the page title (`:70`) and read at runtime through `FrontendApplicationConfigProvider.get()` (`packages/core/src/browser/frontend-application-config-provider.ts:25-31`) by the about dialog, the window title service, the Electron window and the getting-started page. Renaming the product is therefore a manifest key, not a string funnel and not a brand transform.
facts.SEAM-PREFERENCE-DEFAULTS: `theia.frontend.config.preferences` is a plain object of preference id to default value (`examples/browser/package.json:10-13`) — the product-level way to change the default of any upstream preference without touching its schema. Own code that wants the same at run time contributes a `PreferenceContribution` instead (tier 2).
facts.SEAM-PLUGINS: VS Code extensions are the second, unrelated extension mechanism: `theiaPlugins` maps an id to a download URL and `theiaPluginsDir` names where they land (`package.json:127-139`), `theia download:plugins` fetches them (`dev-packages/cli/src/download-plugins.ts:88`) and the running application is pointed at the directory on the command line. A plugin cannot override a core service; it is the seam for editor-level features a product wants to ship pre-installed.
facts.SEAM-RESOURCES: Files of the application directory the manifest points at: the Electron splash screen (`theia.frontend.config.electron.splashScreenOptions.content`, `examples/electron/package.json:15-18`), and whatever a product's packager reads. There is **no icon target table upstream at all** — no `.icns`/`.ico` generation, no installer artwork — so the icons of a distribution are files of the product's own delta and of its packager's configuration.
facts.SEAM-TRANSLATIONS: Own translations are JSON files a `LocalizationContribution` registers (`packages/core/src/node/i18n/localization-contribution.ts:23-25, 56-64`), the way `@theia/core` registers its own `i18n/nls.*.json`. Own strings must use `nls.localize(key, default)`: the lint rule `@theia/localization-check` refuses `nls.localizeByDefault` for any text that is not one of VS Code's own messages (`dev-packages/private-eslint-plugin/rules/localization-check.js:5-8, 29-53`).

tier-2.title: Tier 2 — upstream's own mechanisms for extending the core

facts.SEAM-THEIA-EXTENSION: A package whose `package.json` carries a `theiaExtensions` array is a Theia extension (`dev-packages/application-package/src/extension-package.ts:195-197`); each entry names a module path into `lib/` for one runtime — `frontend`, `frontendElectron`, `backend`, `backendElectron`, `electronMain`, `secondaryWindow`, the preload kinds (`:22-33`) — and each such module default-exports an inversify `ContainerModule`. This is the seam own code lives in, and 77 of the 79 framework packages use it themselves.
facts.SEAM-CONTRIBUTION-POINTS: The additive idiom is a multi-binding to a contribution symbol, read back through `ContributionProvider` (`packages/core/src/common/contribution-provider.ts:20-30`). The symbols a product reaches for first: `FrontendApplicationContribution` (`packages/core/src/browser/frontend-application-contribution.ts:25`), `CommandContribution` (`packages/core/src/common/command.ts:143`), `MenuContribution` (`packages/core/src/common/menu/menu-model-registry.ts:25`), `KeybindingContribution` (`packages/core/src/browser/keybinding.ts:64`), `PreferenceContribution` (`packages/core/src/common/preferences/preference-schema.ts:25`), `ColorContribution` (`packages/core/src/browser/color-application-contribution.ts:27`), `WidgetFactory` (`packages/core/src/browser/widget-manager.ts:23`) and `LocalizationContribution` (`packages/core/src/node/i18n/localization-contribution.ts:23`). None of them needs an upstream edit.
facts.SEAM-REBIND: A service is replaced by `rebind(<Id>).to(...)` or `.toService(...)` inside the own package's `ContainerModule`; it wins because the collector pushes a package after every package it depends on (`dev-packages/application-package/src/extension-package-collector.ts:76-84`), so the own module is loaded after the module that bound the service. **The dependency on the package that binds the service is part of the seam, not decoration**: without it the load order is not guaranteed and the rebind may be overridden itself. 41 upstream packages use the idiom (for example `packages/monaco/src/browser/monaco-frontend-module.ts:94, 110, 153`).
facts.SEAM-NEW-CONTRIBUTION-POINT: Own code may declare a contribution point of its own: a symbol, `bindRootContributionProvider(bind, Symbol)` (`packages/core/src/common/contribution-provider.ts:79-81`), and an injected `ContributionProvider` where it is read. It is the shape upstream uses for every one of its own, and it costs no upstream edit.
facts.SEAM-CHILD-CONTAINERS: A widget or a view may be built in a child container, and a `rebind` inside one is local to it (`packages/outline-view/src/browser/outline-view-frontend-module.ts:44-45`). Whether a child-container rebind reaches what a product wants is **an open question of the spike of 2026-09-09** and was not measured; a seam map that leans on one records the measurement that proved it.

tier-3.title: Tier 3 — the composition of an application

facts.SEAM-DEPENDENCY-LINE: The entry of this family is a JSON key: the application lists the own package in its `dependencies` at the exact monorepo version, the collector finds it by module resolution (`dev-packages/application-package/src/extension-package-collector.ts:32-45, 64`) and the frontend generator emits the container load for every collected module (`dev-packages/application-manager/src/generator/frontend-generator.ts:144`). Transitive Theia extensions are collected too, so depending on a package pulls its extensions in with it.
facts.SEAM-GENERATED-SOURCES-ARE-NOT-A-SEAM: `src-gen/` is written by the generators on every build (`dev-packages/application-package/src/application-package.ts:220-233`) and is never a place to edit. The one generated file that is a seam is `esbuild.mjs` of the application: it is user-editable and only regenerated when it is missing or no longer imports the generated configuration (`dev-packages/application-manager/src/generator/bundler-generator.ts:49-55`), so bundler customization belongs there and nowhere else.
facts.SEAM-APPLICATION-IS-FORKED: Upstream ships three example applications and they are `private` (`examples/browser/package.json:2`); a product's application is a fork of one of them, kept as a directory the delta owns. There is no application generator upstream — `@theia/cli` has `generate`, which writes `src-gen/`, and nothing that scaffolds a project.

tier-4.title: Tier 4 — a hook in an upstream body

facts.SEAM-HOOK-IS-A-LAST-RESORT: Because additions need no edit, a patch of an upstream file in this family means one of a short list: a behaviour with no service identifier and no contribution point behind it, a change to another package's `theiaExtensions`, or a change of the shared `configs/*`. Each is a graft with a named reason (`MI-PATCH-IS-A-GRAFT`), and the seam map says which of the three it is.
facts.SEAM-NO-STRING-FUNNEL: There is no single funnel every user-facing string passes on its way out: `nls.localize` and `nls.localizeByDefault` are two entry points of one namespace (`packages/core/src/common/nls.ts:34-59`), and the VS Code half resolves a message to a key through a vendored metadata file (`:100-140`). A product that wants to rename upstream's own vocabulary does it with its own translation files, not with a transform grafted into a funnel.
facts.SEAM-NEVER-PATCH-THE-PATCHES: `dev-packages/cli/patches/` holds upstream's own patches of `node_modules`, applied on every install by `theia-patch` (`package.json:95`); `package-lock.json` is regenerated by an install; `src-gen/` is generated. None of the three is ever a patch target of a delta.

p.SEAM-TYPE-AUGMENTATION: An own `.d.ts` that augments an exported upstream interface compiles under the package's own `tsconfig.json`, so extra keys of the `theia` section or of a service interface get their type without a patch of an upstream source. The guard is the compiler, and the import must still go through `lib/` and not `src/` — `@theia/no-src-import` refuses the second (`dev-packages/private-eslint-plugin/rules/no-src-import.js:26, 41-47`).

tier-6.title: Tier 6 — build and hygiene registries (the constant graft set)

facts.SEAM-WORKSPACE-GLOBS: The own package has to sit under one of the workspace globs of the root manifest (`package.json:121-126`) or the monorepo's `lerna run` fan-out, its generated tsconfig references and its localization extraction never see it. `packages/<name>` is the slot every framework extension already uses. Changing the globs themselves is a graft of the constant set and needs a decision record.
facts.SEAM-GENERATED-REFERENCES: The `references` array of every `tsconfig.json` is generated from the dependency graph on every install (`scripts/compile-references.js:52-53, 110-119`, run by `postinstall`, `package.json:95`), and CI asserts that installing and building leave the tree unchanged (`./scripts/check_git_status.sh`). So adding a package is **not** a purely additive edit: the tsconfig of every package that depends on it is rewritten, and those rewrites belong to the delta as generated content, not as hand-written patches.
facts.SEAM-PACKAGE-LINT-CONFIG: Linting is type-aware and per package: a package without its own `.eslintrc.js` (extending `configs/build.eslintrc.json` with `tsconfigRootDir`) and its own `tsconfig.json` is not linted at all (`packages/core/.eslintrc.js:1-10`). The own package therefore carries both, and they are files of the delta rather than a graft.
facts.SEAM-LICENCE-HEADER: Every `.ts`/`.tsx` file of a linted package must begin with a header carrying the SPDX line of the framework (`configs/errors.eslintrc.json:105-115`). An own package that carries a different licence either writes a header the rule accepts or overrides that one rule in its own `.eslintrc.js` — the second is a file of the own package, not a graft of upstream.
facts.SEAM-RUNTIME-FOLDERS: The folder names of a package are a closed set and the import direction between them is fixed (`dev-packages/private-eslint-plugin/rules/runtime-import-check.js:25-33, 57-63`): `common`, `browser`, `browser-only`, `node`, `electron-common`, `electron-browser`, `electron-node`, `electron-main`. Own code that keeps those names is checked automatically and needs no entry anywhere; shared libraries — inversify above all — are imported through `@theia/core/shared/*` or `@theia/shared-dependencies` refuses them (`rules/shared-dependencies.js:31, 46, 56`).
facts.SEAM-NLS-EXTRACTION-GLOB: The translation update script hard-codes the glob `./packages/**/{browser,electron-browser,common}/**/*.{ts,tsx}` (`scripts/translation-update.js:29-38`), so an own package under `packages/` is extracted with everything else and one placed elsewhere is not. Whether the CLI's own `--root`/`--files` options serve a package outside that glob is an open question of the spike of 2026-09-09.
facts.SEAM-ROOT-SCRIPTS: The scripts of the root manifest are what a fork's tooling starts: the watch channels of a codkit patch set are two of them (`tsc -b -w` and `theia build --watch`, the pair upstream runs from an application's own `watch` script, `examples/browser/package.json:115-120`). Adding a script is an overlay of the root manifest restricted to `scripts`; touching anything else in that file is a graft of the constant set.

tier-7.title: Tier 7 — the internals of an upstream module

p.SEAM-INTERNALS-ARE-PATCH-EQUIVALENT: Mutating an exported object of an upstream module, depending on the load order beyond the guarantee the dependency graph gives, or reaching into a child container another package built is a patch equivalent wherever the code lives (`MI-INTERNALS-ARE-PATCH-EQUIVALENT`): it needs a contract test, it never throws while a module is evaluated, and the seam map names it as such.

facts.NEVER-TREAT-THE-CATALOGUE-AS-THE-MAP: Never cite this catalogue as the product's seam map: the map is the product's own instance, dated to its pin, naming its interventions.
facts.NEVER-QUOTE-UPSTREAM-CODE-IN-A-STANDARD: Never paste upstream code into a standard or into this catalogue — cite a path and a line.
facts.NEVER-ASSUME-WEBPACK: Never carry knowledge of this family that predates 1.75.0 without re-validating it: webpack bundling was removed in exactly that version and replaced by esbuild (`dev-packages/application-manager/src/generator/bundler-generator.ts:36-47`), and the package manager is npm, not yarn (`lerna.json:3`). A row of a seam map that names either is stale by construction.
